name: Arctic Char Aguachile With Habanero, Jicama, and Lime

ingredients.name: sashimi-grade arctic char fillet
ingredients.prep: skinned and trimmed of any dark flesh

instructions.primary_message: Skin and trim the sashimi-grade arctic char fillet of any dark flesh. Stem, seed, and roughly chop the habanero pepper. Juice the limes. Pick the mint leaves from the stems and roughly chop them. Peel and dice the jicama. Thinly slice the red onion.
instructions.secondary_message:
0.34 kg sashimi-grade arctic char fillet
½ habanero pepper
2 ½ limes
¼ cup packed fresh mint
¼ cup jicama
¼ cup red onion

instructions.primary_message: Split fillet lengthwise along natural division, trimming away center line with any sinew or bones. Then slice the fillet halves crosswise into thin strips. Arrange sliced fish on a large plate and sprinkle all over with salt. Cover with plastic and refrigerate for at least 1 hour and up to 2 hours.
Meanwhile, blend habanero with water in a blender or with an immersion blender until thoroughly blended. Add lime juice and mint and blend until pureed. Season with salt and pepper.
In a mixing bowl, toss arctic char with habanero-lime marinade, jicama, onion, and coriander seed. Season once more with salt and pepper and serve right away with tostadas and avocado.

schema_metadata.keywords: aguachile, ceviche, easy, fish, Latin American, seafood

description: If you love ceviche, then Mexico's aguachile is for you. Traditionally made with raw shrimp, lime juice, chilies, cucumber, and onion, it's served immediately while still totally raw, unlike most other ceviche recipes. In this variation, fresh arctic char is tossed with lime juice, habanero chilies, jicama, coriander seed, and red onion, then served with tostadas and avocado (and if you like, beer or tequila).
notes:
Optional or for serving: Tostadas and fresh avocado, for serving

Optional substitutions: Sea salt → kosher salt

Notes: If you can't find sashimi-grade arctic char, other sashimi-grade fish such as salmon or scallops will work instead. Habanero peppers are extremely spicy: be careful handling them (don't touch your face), and if possible wear latex gloves.
author: Daniel Gritzer
